articles.title: I scanned my machine for the Brotli RCE. Three stacks were exposed — and the patched one still reports the vulnerable version.
articles.excerpt: On Wednesday, Node.js disclosed CVE-2026-111497 — "Node2Shell" — an out-of-bounds write in Google's Brotli decoder that can give a remote, unauthenticated attacker code execution in any process that d…
articles.body: On Wednesday, Node.js disclosed CVE-2026-111497 — "Node2Shell" — an out-of-bounds write in Google's Brotli decoder that can give a remote, unauthenticated attacker code execution in any process that decompresses attacker-controlled Brotli data. By Thursday it had a Python chapter. By Friday, Aikido was calling the wider thing "HTTP2Shell," because the vulnerable decoder is bundled into runtimes, HTTP clients, gateways, and half the internet's plumbing. CVSS v4.0: 9.2. The part that got my attention wasn't the bug. It was this sentence in Aikido's write-up: as of October 23, advisory databases didn't map the CVE to either PyPI package, so pip-audit, Dependabot, and Safety wouldn't flag vulnerable versions.

For Milieu Agency's “Your talent. Your brand. More possibilities.” campaign, the useful question is how to connect a talent story, a brand introduction, a media kit and longer articles while keeping those artifacts accurate. The following workflow is a practical design that another small team can adapt. The code is illustrative and does not imply an undocumented analytics integration. 1.

articles.title: GitHub Actions: A Successful Job Is Not Publication Evidence
articles.excerpt: A scheduled publishing job can finish successfully without creating a public post. That is not necessarily a defect. The job might have selected the other daylight-saving trigger, found no reviewed co…
articles.body: A scheduled publishing job can finish successfully without creating a public post. That is not necessarily a defect. The job might have selected the other daylight-saving trigger, found no reviewed content, performed a dry run, or recognised a publication that already exists. The mistake is treating every successful workflow conclusion as the same business outcome. A useful publisher records what happened to the publication attempt, then keeps that evidence separate from the health of the surrounding job. Separate execution health from delivery A workflow conclusion answers whether its steps met the runner's success conditions. It does not establish that a provider accepted a post, made it public, or returned the destination you expected.

articles.excerpt: I found a small but visible UI bug on Claude's download page, claude.ai/download. Direct visit: the page detects your operating system and shows the matching download options. Arriving from another pa…
articles.body: I found a small but visible UI bug on Claude's download page, claude.ai/download. What happens Direct visit: the page detects your operating system and shows the matching download options. Arriving from another page (for example claude.ai/downloads, then "Download for Linux"): the OS check doesn't run. Every platform's button is shown, and the "Windows (arm64)" and "macOS" buttons render on top of each other. Steps to reproduce Open claude.ai/downloads Click "Download for Linux" Look at the download buttons on claude.ai/download Seen in Chrome on Fedora Linux. Likely cause My guess: the OS detection only runs on a full page load, so an in-app navigation renders the fallback "all platforms" layout, and that layout was never checked with all five buttons visible at once.

articles.title: Go 1.27 Ships a uuid Package. Dropping google/uuid Takes 4 Steps and One NULL Catch
articles.excerpt: Book: The Complete Guide to Go Programming Also by me: Pocket Guides for Developers — the 8-book series My project: Hermes IDE | GitHub — an IDE for developers who ship with Claude Code and other AI c…
articles.body: Book: The Complete Guide to Go Programming Also by me: Pocket Guides for Developers — the 8-book series My project: Hermes IDE | GitHub — an IDE for developers who ship with Claude Code and other AI coding tools Me: xgabriel.com | GitHub Open a Go service's go.mod and there's a good chance github.com/google/uuid is in it. Its latest tag, v1.6.0, dates from January 2024 . Since Go 1.27 shipped on 2026-08-19 , you no longer need it for the common cases. The release notes say it in one line: "The new uuid package generates and parses UUIDs." The import path is just uuid . The swap looks like a find-and-replace on the import line. It mostly is. Two things will fail to compile, which is good, because the compiler finds them for you.

articles.title: 'Star Trek: Strange New Worlds' was afraid to say anything in season of gimmicks
articles.excerpt: The fourth season of "Star Trek: Strange New Worlds" was one giant gimmick: shoving "Trek" into as many genres as possible and often directly adapting classic films from those genres.
articles.body: It didn’t take long for fans to figure out that the fourth season of "Star Trek: Strange New Worlds" was going to be unlike any season of " Star Trek " before it. The entire season was one giant gimmick, and that gimmick was shoving "Trek" into as many genres as possible and often directly adapting classic films from those genres. You could argue that an entire season of gimmick episodes is a bold risk: putting the characters in fun, wacky situations to see how they react. It could be interesting, but the season we got never made the most of the concept. It was all so safe and paint-by-numbers, and, most importantly, it didn't have anything profound or interesting to say. That should trouble any Trekkie.

articles.title: SpaceX launches Starlink satellites from California as Falcon 9 cadence slows (video)
articles.excerpt: SpaceX sent 27 more of its Starlink broadband satellites to orbit today (Oct. 23), in its first Starlink launch in 11 days.
articles.body: SpaceX launched its newest batch of Starlink broadband internet satellites today (Oct. 23) from the California coast. The spacecraft, Starlink Group 15-15, were stacked 27 high inside the payload fairing of a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket , which lifted off from Pad 4E at Vandenberg Space Force Base at 6:48 p.m. EDT (2248 GMT; 3:48 p.m. local time in California). The rocket's first stage booster, designated B1063, executed its main engine cutoff and stage separation about 2.5 minutes into flight, sending the second stage to continue onward to low Earth orbit (LEO). The vehicle's two-piece protective payload fairing was jettisoned just before T+3 minutes. A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket launches 27 Starlink satellites from California on Oct. 23, 2026.

articles.body: 7 Min Read NASA, Partners Accelerate Lander Development for 2028 Moon Missions As NASA returns humans to the lunar surface and establishes a long-term presence on our closest celestial neighbor, the agency and commercial human landing system providers Blue Origin and SpaceX have streamlined the designs and changed both concepts of operations for its future crewed landers.
